# About the Lab

AI Governance Lab is an independent, early-stage research and technology initiative working at the intersection of artificial intelligence, human decision-making, governance, and public policy.

Its mission is to **advance governance and public policy through the design, development, and rigorous evaluation of AI systems**. The Lab aims to connect empirical research with practical technology, without separating the building of AI systems from examining their benefits, risks, and real-world effects.
:::

<div class="about-profile-text">

Caio Velasco graduated first in his class in Mechanical Engineering at the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro (UFRJ), earned a **Master of Public Policy at UCLA** (full scholarship), and undertook first-year doctoral coursework in Economics at Tilburg University. He brings over six years of experience in data science and applied analytics, alongside academic research at UCLA and Royal Holloway (University of London).

His international academic trajectory includes recognition and support from the Lemann Foundation, General Electric Foundation, Yale University, and Club of Rome.

His expertise spans AI and machine learning, statistics, econometrics, causal inference, and modern data platforms. Through **AI Governance Lab**, he brings these disciplines together to advance AI development, evaluation, governance, and public policy.

</div>
:::

## Research & Collaboration

The Lab is open to conversations about independent research, academic collaborations, and carefully scoped applied AI projects with public institutions, researchers, policy organizations, and organizations in regulated sectors.
